title: Python Testing & Debugging: Quick Revision
summary: Night-before revision notes on pytest tests, fixtures, parametrize, monkeypatch and mocking, debugging with breakpoint() and pdb, logging instead of print, and reading tracebacks.

chapters.title: Pytest Mental Model and Assertions
points: pytest collects files named test_*.py or *_test.py, then functions named test_* and methods in Test* classes (no __init__)
A test passes if it finishes without raising; a bare assert is enough, because pytest rewrites assert to show both sides of a failed comparison
pytest.raises(ValueError, match=r'regex') asserts an exception; use 'as exc' and exc.value for details; match uses re.search
Floats: assert 0.1 + 0.2 == pytest.approx(0.3) because exact float equality fails
Mistake: assert (x, 'message') with parentheses is a non-empty tuple, so it is always true

chapters.title: Fixtures and Parametrize
points: @pytest.fixture defines setup; a test requests it by naming it as an argument, and pytest injects the return value
yield fixture: code before yield is setup, code after yield is teardown and runs even if the test fails
scope='function' (default) | 'class' | 'module' | 'session' controls how often it is built; wider scope means shared state and risk of leaks
conftest.py shares fixtures with every test in its directory and below, with no import needed; tmp_path is a built-in per-test temp directory
@pytest.mark.parametrize('a,b,expected', [(1,2,3),(2,3,5)], ids=[...]) runs one test per tuple; stacking two decorators gives the cross product
Mistake: a mutable object in a wide-scope fixture is mutated by one test and breaks the next; keep it function-scoped or copy it

chapters.title: Monkeypatch and Mocking
points: monkeypatch.setattr(obj, 'name', value), setenv, delenv, setitem and chdir are all undone automatically after the test
Patch where the name is looked up, not where it is defined: if app.py does 'from time import sleep', patch 'app.sleep'
unittest.mock.Mock/MagicMock records calls; assert with m.assert_called_once_with(args), m.call_count and m.call_args
m.return_value sets a result, m.side_effect = Exception('x') raises, and side_effect = [1, 2] returns values in order
mocker.patch('pkg.mod.func') from pytest-mock (or the patch context manager) is the same as unittest.mock.patch but cleans up on its own
Mistake: over-mocking tests the mock instead of the code; mock only I/O boundaries such as network, clock and disk, and use autospec=True so wrong signatures fail

chapters.title: Debugging with breakpoint() and pdb
points: breakpoint() drops into pdb at that line; PYTHONBREAKPOINT=0 disables every breakpoint() without editing code
Core pdb commands: n (next line, steps over), s (step into), c (continue), r (run to return), q (quit)
Inspect with p expr, pp expr (pretty print), l (list source), ll (whole function), w (stack), u/d (move up/down a frame), a (show args)
b file:line or b func sets a breakpoint, and tbreak sets a one-shot; cl clears; 'condition 1 x>5' makes breakpoint 1 conditional
pytest --pdb opens pdb on failure; pytest -x --lf stops at the first failure and reruns only last failures; pytest -s is needed so breakpoint() input works with captured output
Mistake: an unknown name typed in pdb is run as Python code, so a variable named n, c or s must be printed with p n
Post-mortem after a crash: python -m pdb script.py or import pdb; pdb.pm()

chapters.title: Logging, Tracebacks and Cheat Sheet
points: Use logging.getLogger(__name__) in each module; log levels in order are DEBUG < INFO < WARNING < ERROR < CRITICAL, and the default threshold is WARNING
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO, format='%(asctime)s %(levelname)s %(name)s: %(message)s') configures the root logger once at the app entry point; libraries must not call it
Pass arguments lazily, logger.info('user %s', uid), not an f-string; logger.exception('msg') inside except logs at ERROR with the full traceback

Read a traceback bottom-up: the last line is the exception type and message, the frame just above it is where it was raised, and 'During handling of the above exception...' marks chained errors (raise X from e keeps the cause)
In tests, the caplog fixture captures logs: assert 'text' in caplog.text, and caplog.set_level(logging.INFO) sets the level
Cheat sheet: pytest -k expr (filter by name) | -x (stop first fail) | -v | -q | --lf | --pdb | -s | --tb=short | -m marker | pytest path::test_name
